speaker: N
text: Every human who has ever lived has lost a fight to a fly. It sees your hand coming from a mile away. It has all the time in the world.

speaker: N
text: But today, one lands on your coffee cup, and you don't swat. You just close your hand. Gotcha.

speaker: N
text: Across the table, your friend's phone slides off the edge. Before he even notices it's falling, you've caught it, put it back, and taken a sip of coffee.

speaker: N
text: He stares at you. You shrug. To you, that phone fell in slow motion.

speaker: N
text: Because your brain now runs ten times faster than everyone else's.

speaker: N
text: What if your reaction time was ten times faster?

speaker: N
text: Normally, it takes you about a quarter of a second to react. Light hits your eyes, your brain decides, and only then do your muscles move.

speaker: N
text: Yours takes two and a half hundredths of a second. That gap between you and everyone else? Let's call it your head start.

speaker: N
text: But here's the catch. Only your brain got the upgrade. Your arms are the same old arms. You're not faster. You're earlier. And it turns out, earlier is almost a superpower.

speaker: N
text: A blink lasts about a tenth of a second. For you, every blink is a full second of darkness. You start blinking a lot less.

speaker: N
text: Toast slides off the plate? Caught, butter side up. Your little sister's ice cream tips off the cone? Caught, and placed right back on top.

speaker: N
text: Online games stop being fair. By the time other players see you, you've already moved. Forty wins in a row. Your inbox fills up with one word. Hacker.

speaker: N
text: Dodgeball becomes a nature documentary. You stand in the middle with your hands in your pockets, and nobody hits you. Not once.

speaker: N
text: And then, things start getting weird.

speaker: N
text: Your brain is burning energy like a gaming computer. You eat five meals a day, and you're still hungry.

speaker: N
text: Conversations feel like loading screens. Your friend starts a sentence, and you've already guessed the ending, answered it in your head, and gotten bored.

speaker: N
text: A ten minute bus ride feels like an hour and a half. A school day feels like a week.

speaker: N
text: So you start finishing people's sentences. Then their jokes. And one day, your friend just stops telling you jokes.

speaker: N
text: Being early for everything, it turns out, is a lonely way to live.

speaker: N
text: But one Saturday afternoon, being early is the only thing that matters.

speaker: N
text: The train platform is packed. Your friend, your little sister, and the red balloon she's been carrying all day.

speaker: N
text: The string slips out of her hand. She follows it. One step. Two. Toward the edge. And the express train that doesn't stop here.

speaker: N
text: Everyone else will see it in a quarter of a second. You see it now.

speaker: N
text: And here's the thing about a head start. You can't run faster than anyone. Your legs are normal legs. All you get is time to think.

speaker: N
text: So you think. Grab her arm? Too far. Shout? She won't hear you over the train. You get one move.

speaker: N
text: You don't reach for your sister. You reach for the balloon.

speaker: N
text: The string stops. She stops. She looks up at the balloon, then at you.

speaker: N
text: By the time anyone else on the platform reacts, it's already over. Nobody even knows anything happened. Except your friend. He saw the whole thing.

speaker: N
text: And for the first time in months, he isn't looking at you like a hacker. He just says, okay. Tell me what it's like.

speaker: N
text: So you tell him. Slowly. You let him finish his sentences. You laugh at the end of his joke, even though you saw it coming a mile away.

speaker: N
text: And when a fly lands on your coffee cup, you just watch it. You have all the time in the world. So you let it go.

speaker: N
text: What would you do with a quarter second head start? Tell us in the comments. And if you'd have reached for the balloon too, subscribe for more what ifs.
